introduction.title: Troubleshooting Guide
introduction.description: For a first local install, use the guarded order: create .env.local, run npm run local:setup, then npm run local:check, npm run dev, and (when needed) npm run worker. local:setup starts the owned dependencies itself; local:up is only for restarting an already-initialized profile during recovery. Do not substitute raw Compose, Prisma, PostgreSQL, or Valkey commands. A local start is not an end-to-end verification; test the workflow you need. If the problem persists, capture the guarded command output and submit an Issue.

categories.name: Installation & Startup
categories.description: Issues related to installation, configuration, and startup

issues.title: Node.js Version Incompatibility
Problems: Node.js version error when running yarn dev
Some dependency packages fail to install
solutions: Ensure Node.js version ≥ 18.18
Use nvm or corepack to manage Node.js version
Run `node --version` to check current version
If using corepack, run `corepack enable` to enable

issues.title: Yarn Dependency Installation Failure
solutions: Check network connection, may need to configure proxy
Clear cache: `yarn cache clean`
Delete node_modules and yarn.lock, reinstall
Use corepack to manage Yarn: `corepack prepare yarn@1.22.22 --activate`

issues.title: Managed Local Setup Failure
Problems: Guarded local dependency services cannot start
solutions: Confirm .env.local was copied from .env.local.example and AUTH_SECRET was replaced; local:setup reports configuration failures before it starts containers.
Ensure Docker Desktop is running, but do not run project Compose commands directly.
Check whether unrelated processes occupy the owned loopback ports 55432, 56379, 59002, or 59003.
After correcting the cause, retry `npm run local:setup`; after it succeeds, run `npm run local:check`.
Do not run volume-removal or raw Compose cleanup commands. For a production incident, use the production runbook instead of the local runner.

issues.title: Environment Variable Configuration Error
Problems: Cannot connect to database after application startup
solutions: Create .env.local from .env.local.example; do not reuse .env or .env.production.
For a fresh profile, run `npm run local:setup`, then `npm run local:check` instead of validating database or Valkey URLs by hand.
Replace AUTH_SECRET in .env.local with a random local value.
With LOCAL_ALLOW_REMOTE_AI=no, remote-model functions are expected to be unavailable; enable them only with local development credentials.
Restart through `npm run dev` or `npm run worker` after changing the local profile.

issues.title: Database Connection Failure
Problems: Error when application starts: cannot connect to database
solutions: For a fresh profile, run `npm run local:setup`; it starts owned dependencies, applies the local schema, and creates demo data.
After setup succeeds, run `npm run local:check` to verify that the database is the owned deeptrans_local instance.
If an already-initialized profile's dependencies stopped, use `npm run local:up` rather than a raw Compose command, then run `npm run local:check`.
Read the guarded command output rather than connecting with psql or another shell client.
For production database diagnosis, use the approved production procedure, not the local commands.

issues.title: Local Migration or Setup Failure
solutions: Retry `npm run local:setup`; it owns the complete first-install path and starts dependencies itself.
After a successful setup, run `npm run local:check` to verify the isolated profile and migration state.
Do not run raw Prisma migrate, deploy, or reset commands against a shell-provided DATABASE_URL.
Keep the guarded-command error output for diagnosis instead of editing migration state manually.
Only start the app with `npm run dev` after local setup succeeds.

issues.title: Local Data Inspection Is Unavailable
Problems: The local app is running but expected data is absent
A direct database inspection tool is unavailable
solutions: Run `npm run local:check` to confirm the owned local database and migration state.
Use the supported application screens to inspect project and memory data.
Do not start Prisma Studio or another direct client with an arbitrary environment URL.
Escalate a required production inspection through the approved production access procedure.

categories.name: Valkey & Queue Issues
categories.description: Valkey connection and BullMQ queue related issues

issues.title: Valkey Connection Failure
Problems: Valkey connection error when application starts
solutions: Run `npm run local:check` to validate the owned local Valkey service.
Use `npm run local:up` when the local dependencies are not running.
Start or restart the guarded Worker with `npm run worker` after the check passes.
Do not test, flush, or inspect a shell-provided Redis URL with redis-cli.
Use the Worker output and application job state to diagnose the queue.

issues.title: Queue Task Backlog
Problems: Number of tasks in queue keeps growing
Worker processing speed cannot keep up
solutions: Confirm the guarded Worker is running with `npm run worker`.
Run `npm run local:check` before assuming a queue or Valkey failure.
Review the in-app workflow and job history for the affected task.
Do not clear Valkey with FLUSHDB or another broad Redis command; it can remove unrelated state.
For persistent failures, keep the Worker output and escalate with the task identifier.

issues.title: Task Execution Failure
solutions: Review the terminal output from `npm run worker`.
Check if task data format is correct
Verify PostgreSQL/pgvector/PGroonga, Valkey, object storage, MinerU PDF parsing, and API keys are healthy
Check if API keys and configuration are correct
Use the in-app task history; do not query Valkey keys directly from a shell.

issues.title: pgvector Connection Failure
solutions: Run `npm run local:setup` to apply the local schema and create required extensions.
After setup succeeds, run `npm run local:check` to verify the owned PostgreSQL instance and migration state.
Verify the local profile rather than manually changing DATABASE_URL or extension state.
Review the guarded app or Worker output for the failing workflow.
Do not inspect or alter embeddings with direct SQL from a local shell.

issues.title: Translation Memory Embedding Missing
solutions: Start a missing-vector backfill job for the target memory; do not re-import text rows that already exist.
With LOCAL_ALLOW_REMOTE_AI=no, model-backed embeddings are expected to be unavailable.
If embeddings are intentionally enabled, keep provider settings in .env.local and validate the profile with `npm run local:check`.
Do not use direct SQL to change extension or vector state.

issues.title: Vector Dimension Mismatch
solutions: Check the embedding configuration; translation memory uses a fixed 2048-dimensional contract
Confirm the migration created the halfvec(2048) expression HNSW index
Run an explicit re-embedding migration before changing embedding models
Verify vector generation code and database schema are aligned

categories.name: PDF Parsing Issues
categories.description: MinerU online PDF parsing and local fallback issues

issues.title: PDF Parsing Fails
Problems: PDF files cannot be processed after upload
Parsing tasks remain in PENDING status
solutions: Review the terminal output from `npm run dev` and, for queued parsing, `npm run worker`.
Verify MINERU_API_MODE is agent, standard, or precise
For agent mode, verify MINERU_AGENT_BASE_URL is reachable
For standard/precise mode, configure MINERU_API_TOKEN and verify MINERU_API_BASE_URL
If the online parser is unavailable, set MINERU_DISABLE=true to use local text extraction intentionally
Check whether the PDF is corrupted or outside supported formats

issues.title: PDF Parsing Timeout
Problems: Large file parsing takes too long
solutions: Current upload limit is 10MB; reduce or split larger PDFs before upload
Increase MINERU_TIMEOUT_MS or MINERU_POLL_INTERVAL_MS for slow parsing tasks
Use MINERU_PAGE_RANGE to parse a smaller page range first
Check MinerU service availability and network access from the app container

categories.name: Object Storage Issues
categories.description: MinIO or Tencent COS storage service related issues

issues.title: Object Storage Connection Failure
solutions: Verify STORAGE_TYPE is minio or cos
For MinIO, verify STORAGE_ENDPOINT, STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY, STORAGE_SECRET_KEY, and STORAGE_BUCKET
For Tencent COS, verify COS_SECRET_ID, COS_SECRET_KEY, COS_BUCKET, and COS_REGION
Check that the bucket exists and the credential has object read/write permissions

issues.title: File Upload Failure
Problems: Documents cannot be saved after upload
solutions: For the managed local MinIO service, check disk space and the local runner output
For Tencent COS, check bucket quota, region, credentials, and CORS/policy settings
Check file size limits
Verify STORAGE_TYPE and object storage configuration

issues.title: Worker Cannot Start
Problems: The guarded local Worker reports errors
solutions: Run `npm run local:check` to validate the local profile and dependencies
Verify the guarded Valkey service through the check
Review the terminal output from `npm run worker`
Check Node.js version
Verify dependencies are correctly installed
Check build artifacts with `npm run build:worker`

issues.title: Worker Not Processing Tasks
Problems: Tasks in queue but Worker does not consume
solutions: Check if Worker is running normally
Verify queue name configuration is correct
Check error messages in Worker logs
Confirm Worker is subscribed to correct queue
Restart Worker service

issues.title: Slow Page Loading
solutions: Check database query performance, analyze using Prisma Studio
Optimize database indexes
Check if Valkey cache is working normally
View browser network panel to analyze request time
Check server resource usage (CPU, memory)

issues.title: Authentication Failure
solutions: Check if AUTH_SECRET is set
Verify NEXTAUTH_URL configuration is correct
Clear browser Cookies and LocalStorage
Check NextAuth configuration
View authentication errors in server logs

issues.title: API Route Errors
solutions: Check if route files exist
Verify API paths are correct
View Next.js build logs
Check middleware configuration
Verify request methods and parameters

tips.title: View Logs
tips.description: Use guarded local process output; production logs belong to the production runbook

tips.title: Check Service Status
tips.description: Verify that the local services are the owned isolated dependencies
commands: Do not probe an arbitrary database or cache URL from a shell

tips.title: Database Debugging
tips.description: Validate the managed local database before inspecting application state
commands: Use supported application screens for local data inspection

tips.title: Queue Debugging
tips.description: Inspect queue state through the guarded Worker and application workflow history
commands: Review the in-app task and workflow history
Do not run redis-cli FLUSHDB, KEYS, or GET against a shell-provided URL
